# GEO report: trailhead **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 46–54/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 10.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 46. High = (10.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 54. The site renders only in the browser, so the served HTML is nearly empty. Every page shares one title and description, and the Guides page is hidden from search. The one unknown is the canonical tag, which needs your real domain. All results are read from code. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Make pages render on the server (3 points lost) - **Why it matters:** with browser-only rendering, crawlers that don't run JavaScript get an empty page instead of your walks and guides. - **Where:** `nuxt.config.ts:2` - **What the code says:** `ssr: false,` - **Size:** Small (remove it, or prerender the routes) - **Score after this:** 59–67 ### 2. Make the robots.txt Sitemap line an absolute URL (2 points lost) - **Why it matters:** the Sitemap line must be a full URL, and a relative one may be ignored, so crawlers may not find the sitemap. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4` - **What the code says:** `Sitemap: /sitemap.xml` - **Size:** Small (use `https://trailhead.example/sitemap.xml`, or your real domain) - **Score after this:** 54–63 ### 3. Make the path to Trail guides a real link (2 points lost) - **Why it matters:** the only route to `/guides` is a button that runs JavaScript. Crawlers follow `` links, so they may never discover the page. - **Where:** `pages/index.vue:8` - **What the code says:** `` - **Size:** Small (use ``) - **Score after this:** 54–63 ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt valid and small | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, valid lines | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers allowed | Clear | Only `Disallow: /admin`; assumed you want to be found | | GEO-014 | Routes indexable | Problem | `/guides` is noindex (`server/middleware/headers.ts:3`); `/` is fine (1 of 2) | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical | Can't tell | No canonical set anywhere; needs your real domain | | GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Problem | `nuxt.config.ts:2`, both routes | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD valid | Not applicable | None in the project | | GEO-011 | Sitemap discoverable | Problem | `public/robots.txt:4` is a relative Sitemap line | | GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Problem | `lang` is set, but one shared title and description (`app.vue:2`, `nuxt.config.ts:6`), both routes | | GEO-016 | Links in server HTML | Problem | `/guides` reached only by `pages/index.vue:8` | | GEO-017 | Snippet restrictions | Clear | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0` found | | GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | Read `app.vue` and the three pages: no images, button has text, title set | | GEO-101 | App association files | Not applicable | No app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only) | Not applicable | Not present; not scored | | GEO-102 | App structured data (info only) | Not applicable | Not scored | ## Other problems found - **The sitemap lists a page the server marks noindex.** `public/sitemap.xml:4` has `https://trailhead.example/guides`, but `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` sets `setResponseHeader(event, 'X-Robots-Tag', 'noindex');` for `/guides`. This looks like a mistake, since it's your main content page. Remove the header rule, or remove the page from the sitemap if you meant to hide it. - **The `/admin` rule is a bit redundant.** `pages/admin.vue:2` sets noindex while `public/robots.txt:2` also has `Disallow: /admin`. A crawler blocked by robots.txt can't see the noindex tag, but this looks deliberate, so I left it alone. ## Worth considering - **Show the trail guides on the Guides page:** `pages/guides.vue:4`: `

Routes graded from easy to strenuous.

`. The page promises graded routes but lists none. Adding each route with its name, grade and length as text would give readers and machines something to quote. - **Give each route its own page:** if you add a list of routes, a page per route, such as `/guides/`, could each have their own title, description and sitemap entry. - **Give the home page some text:** `pages/index.vue:7`: `

Walks across the Peak District

`. The home page has only a heading and a button. A short description of the walks, with links to the guides, would tell visitors what the site offers. - **Write per-page titles and descriptions:** `app.vue:2`: `useHead({ title: 'Trailhead' })`. A title like "Trail guides – Peak District walks | Trailhead", plus a page-specific `useHead` description, would say what each page is. - **Add a canonical tag:** nothing in `nuxt.config.ts` sets the site's URL or any `rel="canonical"`. Declare your real domain and add one absolute canonical per page. - **Label the site's identity:** `WebSite` or `Organization` JSON-LD with the name "Trailhead" and its URL would state who the site is in a machine-readable way. - **Generate the sitemap instead of hand-keeping it:** `public/sitemap.xml` is a static file. A Nuxt sitemap module would keep it in step with the routes and could add `` dates. ## Can't tell from code - **GEO-015 (canonical):** no canonical is set, and the only domain in the code is `trailhead.example`. Tell me your real domain and I can settle this. - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs `, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Headers set outside the repo:** hosting may add `X-Robots-Tag` or other headers that this code doesn't show. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI search tools to find the site, and there is no `geo.config.json`. - `/admin` is deliberately hidden from search. - I sampled `/` and `/guides` as the important routes. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-003`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
